simba.Modules.plotting.ring module

Plots for the two nonlinear ring studies: dynamic aperture and frequency map.

Both are magnitude plots – turns survived, and a diffusion index – so both use a single sequential hue rather than a rainbow, which keeps the ordering readable and survives colour-vision deficiency and greyscale printing. viridis is the default that Modules.Beams.plot already uses.

The one categorical distinction, survived against lost, is carried by marker shape and a legend entry, never by colour alone: on a map whose whole point is the boundary between the two, a reader who cannot separate the hues would lose the result entirely.

CMAP = <matplotlib.colors.ListedColormap object>

Sequential, perceptually uniform and CVD-safe; matches Beams.plot.

SURVIVED_COLOUR = '#2a4858'

A single dark step for survivors. They all survived the same number of turns, so there is no magnitude among them to encode – the shape and the legend carry the distinction, and the colour axis is left for the losses.

plot_amplitude_map(footprint, axes=None, title='Amplitude map', **kwargs)[source]

The same diffusion index against starting amplitude rather than tune.

The companion to plot_frequency_map(): one says which resonance a particle is on, this says where in the machine aperture it started.

Return type:

matplotlib.axes.Axes

Parameters:

title (str)

plot_dynamic_aperture(aperture, turns, axes=None, title='Dynamic aperture', **kwargs)[source]

Survival over the starting-amplitude grid.

Parameters:

  • aperture (list) – (x, y, turns_survived) as run_dynamic_aperture() returns.

  • turns (int) – Turns asked for, so survivors can be told from losses. A survivor reaches turns - 1: Ocelot numbers turns from zero, and testing against turns would mark every particle lost.

  • axes (matplotlib.axes.Axes | None) – Drawn into if given, otherwise a new figure.

  • title (str)

Return type:

matplotlib.axes.Axes

plot_frequency_map(footprint, axes=None, order=4, title='Frequency map', **kwargs)[source]

Tune footprint coloured by the diffusion index.

Parameters:

  • footprint (list) – (x, y, tune_x, tune_y, D) as run_frequency_map() returns.

  • order (int) – Highest resonance order drawn; 0 draws none.

  • title (str)

Return type:

matplotlib.axes.Axes

resonance_lines(axes, order=4, **kwargs)[source]

Overlay m*Qx + n*Qy = p up to |m| + |n| <= order.

Drawn recessively and thinner with increasing order, because a frequency map is read by which line a feature sits on – the lines are reference, not data.

Parameters:

order (int)

Return type:

None
